newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges world to learn from Sino-Russia pact.
newsitem.headline: China urges world to learn from Sino-Russia pact.

text.p: China's Communist Party mouthpiece, the People's Daily, on Sunday hailed President Jiang Zemin's visit to Russia as a triumph and lauded his joint declaration with Moscow as a model for new world order.
"As the world situation develops, people will see more and more clearly the great contribution President Jiang has made in his visit and the significance of the tour," the editorial said.

Jiang flew home on Saturday after a five-day visit to Russia during which he signed a treaty with President Boris Yeltsin and the presidents of Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan on cutting troop levels along the old Sino-Soviet border.

Jiang and Yeltsin also issued a declaration outlining their vision of the post-Cold War world and opposition to claims by any country for world leadership -- a clear, albeit implicit, reference to the United States.
The People's Daily picked up the theme of a new world order in its editorial titled: "A Visit of Great Significance and Far-reaching Impact" that marked Jiang's return.

The commentary was accompanied by a front-page picture showing Jiang, who also heads the Communist Party as well as China's army, shaking hands with other Politburo members on his return. The newspaper carried a half-page montage of photographs from Jiang's Russian tour.
Jiang's trip had opened a new chapter in the history of Sino-Russian relations, the editorial said.
The new relationship was a model for other countries as to how to develop ties amid a new multipolarity in the world after the end of the Cold War, the People's Daily said.
"The new international order is a new model for international relations," it said. "No country should be allowed to impose its social system and ideology on others."
"There is no doubt that only by establishing the new international order, will the world we live in enjoy lasting peace and tranquillity," it said.

Moscow and Beijing had said they see the treaty and the declaration as part of a new relationship of "partnership aimed at strategic cooperation in the 21st century," but both sides have ruled out a closer union.

Sino-Russian ties have improved rapidly since the mid-1980s. Their alliance of the 1950s collapsed amid rivalry for leadership of the communist world into more than two decades of hostility with several bloody territorial clashes.
"(The declaration's) implementation will prove that relations between the two countries are full of vitality and will stand the test of time," the editorial said.
The newspaper did not hesitate to issue a thinly veiled reference to the United States, which Jiang is due to visit in November.
"The time when a few big powers or power blocs could monopolise world affairs and dictate the fate of others has gone for ever," the newspaper said.
"Relations between and among big powers are seeing a major shift," it said.
The United States on Thursday denied Washington sought "domination or a unipolar world" but asserted that the U.S. wielded a special power and influence around the globe.
